snapshot: WHO European Region. One of the largest funders of WHO and of the Global Fund, but critics say it has no working global health strategy: seven ministries share responsibility and the development ministry ended bilateral health cooperation in January 2026.

agenda.title: Funding for global health under pressure
agenda.text: Germany has been the largest or second-largest WHO donor and funds the Global Fund (EUR 1 billion for 2026 to 2028) and Gavi (EUR 600 million over five years). Voluntary WHO contributions are being cut, only about a third of the US$262 million pledged at the 2024 World Health Summit has been budgeted, and the health ministry's international operations fund would fall 15.3% in the 2027 draft. The Bundestag settles the budget in late November.

agenda.title: No ministerial coordinator for global health
agenda.text: According to Health Policy Watch, Germany has no working global health strategy, no ministerial coordinator and no Bundestag subcommittee on global health, which lapsed after the 2025 election. The 2020 strategy runs to 2030 but its mid-term review set no clear milestones.

agenda.title: Domestic prevention and care reform
agenda.text: The health ministry is running a nationwide vaccination action week (9 to 15 November 2026), and the Bundestag has held a first reading of a long-term care reform bill (Pflegeneuordnungsgesetz).
